scope: A1 pilot task windows, proxy-observed POST /prompt traffic and direct read-only history checks for indexed prompt IDs
interpretation: No duplicate submissions or extra starts are evident in captured proxy traffic and queried terminal history for indexed handles; with the explicit assumption that all task POST traffic traversed the proxy and no same-handle execution was overwritten in history, a task-scoped duplicate count of zero is supported. Without these assumptions the total duplicate execution count is unobservable and remains null. B has no independent live WebSocket start trace; its start evidence is terminal history, not a live observation. A has 20 live starts for its indexed IDs.
limitations: The passive relay observes only traffic directed through it, not direct calls to ComfyUI or traffic from other clients. Both recorded launch configurations target the relay; these settings alone cannot prove absence of bypass.
A terminal history record is a current per-handle view, not a guaranteed append-only count of every execution if the same handle is reused or history is overwritten.
Counts describe the stated time windows, not subsequent runs or all activity on the ComfyUI instance.
Unobserved errors and executions outside the observer are not ruled out; missing live B WebSocket events do not mean B did not execute.
